outcome: Esnault and Groechenig (arXiv:2606.16873, June 2026) prove the p-curvature conjecture for a newly-defined class of higher-dimensional local systems ('privileged local systems') via a proof strategy avoiding middle convolution, settling this case while the general conjecture remains open; no AI involvement was found in this or any other result located.
summary: The frozen Wikipedia bullet states the p-curvature conjecture in its classical form: a local-global principle for linear ODEs (finite monodromy after a finite étale cover iff p-curvature vanishes for almost all primes). The conjecture remains open in general, but I found a genuine case settled in the window: Esnault and Groechenig, 'The Grothendieck-Katz Conjecture for privileged local systems' (arXiv:2606.16873, submitted 2026-06-15), define 'privileged local systems' on smooth quasi-projective varieties in any dimension — a generalization of Katz's classical notion of physical rigidity on opens of P^1 — and prove the conjecture holds for this class, via a new proof avoiding middle convolution. This restricts the stated question to a specific class of local systems and settles it there, so it is a case (§3.1), not a variant, and is classified `partial` with direction `confirmed` (the conjecture's prediction held for this class). I also found and ruled out other candidate events: (1) Movasati's 'Grothendieck-Katz conjecture' (arXiv:2403.11829, March 2024), which reformulated the conjecture under a stronger hypothesis, was withdrawn in v3 (Feb 2025) and folded into a larger paper, 'Leaf schemes and Hodge loci' (arXiv:2502.19988) — I could not fully confirm from the fetched content whether the folded version still makes a live claim about the classical conjecture, but since the standalone reformulation was withdrawn and superseded, I do not treat it as a standing event; (2) Lam and Litt, 'p-Curvature and Non-Abelian Cohomology' (arXiv:2601.07933, Jan 2026), prove a non-abelian analogue of the p-curvature conjecture for isomonodromy foliations on moduli of flat bundles — this changes the stated hypotheses (non-abelian setting, different objects) rather than restricting the classical linear-ODE question, so under §3.1 it is a related problem, not a case, and does not by itself move this record; (3) Fürnsinn and Pannier, 'An Effective Version of the p-Curvature Conjecture for Order One Differential Equations' (arXiv:2510.00892, Oct 2025), build an effective/computable version and SageMath algorithm on top of Honda's pre-existing proof for order-one equations — this is `progress`-grade (an effectivization of an already-solved case) and is subsumed by the more substantial Esnault-Groechenig result as the decisive event, so I did not create a separate record for it. No source among these mentions AI, machine learning, or automated theorem-proving tools in any capacity — all are traditional algebraic-geometry/arithmetic arguments by named human authors.
competing_reading: One could argue the Esnault-Groechenig result is itself a 'related problem' rather than a 'case', since privileged local systems are a genuinely new definition rather than a pre-existing restriction of the classical hypothesis space. Against this: the paper explicitly frames privileged local systems as a generalization of Katz's own notion of physical rigidity (already a recognized sufficient condition invoked in the classical literature on this conjecture), and the local systems covered are honest instances of the objects quantified over in the original statement (flat connections/local systems on a variety), not a different kind of object or a differently-posed question. I classify it as a case, but flag the alternative.
what_would_settle_it: A close reading of how 'privileged local systems' relates set-theoretically to the class of local systems the classical conjecture quantifies over (i.e., whether every privileged local system is an admissible instance of the general conjecture's hypotheses) would settle whether this is a case or a variant. Also, obtaining the full text of the folded Movasati paper (arXiv:2502.19988) to see whether it still asserts a proof/reformulation bearing on the classical conjecture would clarify whether that thread constitutes an additional (withdrawn-then-superseded) event.
